where: Section 1, self-attention paragraph and formula note
problem: Q, K and V are all said to be n × dk matrices, but dk is defined as the query/key width. In the standard formulation Q and K are n × dk while V is n × dv, and the attention output has width dv. The chapter never defines dv or says dv = dk, so a student may think the value vectors must share the key width.
fix: Write 'Q and K are n × dk and V is n × dv, where dv is the value width', or state explicitly 'take dv = dk throughout, so all three are n × dk'.

problem: 'The upper triangle of the score matrix is set to −∞' is ambiguous. The diagonal entry (the token attending to itself) must not be masked; if a student masks the whole upper triangle including the diagonal, the token loses its own value.
fix: Say 'every score above the diagonal, that is, for future positions j > i, is set to −∞; the diagonal is kept'.

problem: 'QKT' is written without the transpose, while the formula uses QKᵀ. The same quantity is written two ways, which can confuse a reader scanning the note.
fix: Write QKᵀ in the explanatory sentence too.

problem: [SEP] is described only as appearing between sentences. BERT also appends [SEP] after the last token of each segment, so the full input is [CLS] A [SEP] B [SEP].
fix: State that every segment ends with [SEP]: [CLS] A [SEP] B [SEP], or [CLS] A [SEP] for a single sentence.
